clue.text: Reads and records for the police

blocks.note: to con is an old word for to study or read over carefully
tables are lists of recorded figures

explanation.surface: Someone reads and keeps records on behalf of the police force.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reads and records' looks like a police clerk's duties; each word instead supplies a piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Constables are ordinary uniformed officers, so collectively they stand for the police force.

clue.text: Animal with firm back bearing a great deal

indicators.note: going back means reading the abbreviation from right to left

blocks.note: Co. is the abbreviation for company, a firm
east is a compass bearing
a lot means a great deal

explanation.surface: An animal carries a heavy load on the back of a sturdy frame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Firm back' reads as a sturdy spine, but firm is the company and back turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: The ocelot is a spotted wild cat of Central and South America, a specific example of an animal.

clue.text: Harsh trend - it's quite wrong

indicators.note: letters that are quite wrong are out of order and need putting right

blocks.note: the eight letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone harshly condemns a fashion trend as completely mistaken.
explanation.definitionFit: A strident voice or tone is loud, grating and jarring, which is to say harsh.

clue.text: At a late hop about giving service

blocks.note: taken as written
ten o'clock at night is a late hour
a hop is an informal dance

explanation.surface: Staff at a late-night dance are busy waiting on the guests.
explanation.walkthrough: The loosest piece: a late hop is read as a dance at about ten o'clock, so 'about' rounds the hour rather than signalling a container.
explanation.definitionFit: Attendance is the act of waiting on or serving someone, as a servant or nurse gives attendance.

clue.text: Many won't work on a ship without cover

blocks.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty, a large number
someone idle does no work
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: Lots of sailors refuse to work aboard an unsheltered vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Many' as a Roman numeral (L, D, C, M) is a standard trick.
explanation.definitionFit: Something lidless has no lid, the top that would cover it.

clue.text: In Spain there isn't one bridge

indicators.note: saying something isn't there tells you to leave it out of the country's name

blocks.note: the country, taken as written
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Spain is said to have not one single bridge.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the I (one) out of SPAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A span is the stretch of a bridge between supports, and as a verb or noun it means to bridge a gap.

clue.text: Diffident about losing interest

blocks.note: re means about, concerning
growing tired of something is losing interest in it

explanation.surface: A shy person who is starting to lose interest in things.
explanation.definitionFit: Retiring describes a shy, reserved person who avoids company, just as a diffident one lacks confidence.

clue.text: President flushing over not being backed

indicators.note: something backed is moved in reverse, so the word is read right to left

blocks.note: flushing out is washing
taken as written

explanation.surface: A president blushes because his campaign has lost its backers.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'over' places the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: George Washington was the first President of the United States.

clue.text: A steep requirement for converting foreign currency

indicators.note: converting the letters means changing them into a different form

blocks.note: the six letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Changing money abroad comes with a steep charge.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface of steep conversion charges sits neatly on the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The peseta was Spain's monetary unit before the euro, so it was money from abroad for a British traveller.

clue.text: Satisfied about blunder made with teeth

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word wraps around the other

blocks.note: sated means satisfied, filled up
to err is to make a mistake

explanation.surface: Someone is pleased about a slip-up involving false teeth.
explanation.definitionFit: A serrated edge, like a bread knife, is notched with a row of small sharp points like teeth.

clue.text: Get depressed when left suffering

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for left
anguish is severe suffering

explanation.surface: Someone sinks into gloom after being abandoned in pain.
explanation.definitionFit: To languish is to pine, droop or lose spirit, close to becoming dejected or low.

clue.text: Some nasty, even unsightly, swelling

indicators.note: some means only part of the following words is wanted

blocks.note: the letters run across the two words
surface padding that completes the picture of an ugly lump

explanation.surface: A description of an ugly, unpleasant lump.
explanation.definitionFit: A stye is a small inflamed lump on the edge of the eyelid, a kind of swelling.

clue.text: A good man - and yet coming to a stop

blocks.note: St, saint, is a good man
taken as written
still means yet, nevertheless

explanation.surface: A virtuous man nevertheless comes to a halt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coming to a stop' looks like a single phrase meaning halting; only 'a stop' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A standstill is a complete halt, a state in which all motion has ceased.

clue.text: Prudence, given no credit, is upset

indicators.note: something upset is knocked over and disordered

blocks.note: the ten letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Prudence is upset at being refused credit, as if she were a person.
explanation.walkthrough: Prudence reads as a woman's name, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Discretion is careful judgement in speech and action, the same caution that prudence names.

clue.text: "— is but want of power to sin" (Dryden)

blocks.clueFragment: — is but want of power to sin
blocks.note: the quotation with one word missing
the source: John Dryden, the seventeenth-century English poet

explanation.walkthrough: A fill-in-the-blank: Dryden's line from Aureng-Zebe runs 'Repentance is but want of power to sin', a cynical view of contrition.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing word names sincere regret and remorse for past wrongdoing.

clue.text: A solvent - one to use with pitch

blocks.note: an ace is the one in a pack of cards
the pitch of a sound is its tone

explanation.surface: A chemist recommends a solvent for removing pitch, the sticky tar.
explanation.walkthrough: Pitch looks like tar that a solvent would dissolve; here it is musical pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: Acetone is a volatile liquid widely used to dissolve paints, varnish and nail polish.

clue.text: Irresponsible conduct of a dunderhead in flight

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter
in places one thing inside another

blocks.note: flight from danger is escape
taken as written
the head of dunder, its first letter

explanation.surface: A fool behaves recklessly while running away.
explanation.walkthrough: Dunderhead looks like one word meaning fool, but it splits into dunder and head.
explanation.definitionFit: An escapade is a reckless or mischievous adventure, an act of carefree misbehaviour.

clue.text: Honourable, genteel, quiet Conservatives

blocks.note: U means upper-class, the genteel usage in Nancy Mitford's U and non-U
p (piano) is the musical mark for quiet
Conservatives are the political right

explanation.surface: A description of respectable, refined, soft-spoken Tories.
explanation.definitionFit: An upright person is honest and morally principled, a person of integrity.

clue.text: Inn later completely reconstructed inside

indicators.note: something completely reconstructed has been rebuilt in a new form

blocks.note: the eight letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A pub that was later wholly rebuilt on the inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inside' sits at the end looking like part of the building story; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Internal means situated on the inside, as opposed to external.

clue.text: The climber's sole aid

blocks.note: surface reading: the one and only help a mountaineer has
setter's reading: sole is the underside of a boot, where this spiked climbing aid is strapped

explanation.walkthrough: Sole looks like 'only' but means the bottom of a boot.
explanation.definitionFit: A crampon is a metal plate with spikes fixed to a boot for gripping ice when climbing.

clue.text: Figure of Parisian once hard to get into shape

indicators.note: getting into shape means being formed anew, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: de is French for of
the eight letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A Parisian woman's figure was once difficult to get into shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Figure' and 'shape' suggest fitness; the figure is geometric.
explanation.definitionFit: A decahedron is a solid geometric figure with ten plane faces.

clue.text: A revolutionary act?

definitions.note: read as a noun phrase: a single revolution, one rotation

blocks.note: first meaning: one revolution, a rotation
second meaning: a performer's slot on a variety bill

explanation.walkthrough: Read together, the words suggest an act of rebellion; the question mark warns that revolutionary means going round, not revolt.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means one rotation about an axis, and in theatre it is one performer's piece on a music-hall programme.

clue.text: Fruit for artist's home

blocks.note: RA, Royal Academician, is an artist
the 's read as is
at home means in

explanation.surface: A bowl of fruit set out at a painter's house.
explanation.definitionFit: A raisin is a dried grape, a type of fruit.

clue.text: Having to carry a seat some servicemen find a beastly nuisance

indicators.note: to carry something is to hold it within

blocks.note: having to, the to joining the containing word
a pew is a church seat
RM, the Royal Marines, are some servicemen

explanation.surface: Soldiers forced to lug a seat around find it a confounded nuisance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Having to' looks like obligation, but the to is a word that holds the seat. 'Beastly' is fair, since this nuisance really is an animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A tapeworm is a parasitic flatworm living in the gut, a creature that is an unwelcome pest.

clue.text: Propellers going round are changing the direction

indicators.note: changing the direction means swapping one compass point for another

blocks.note: O is a round shape
taken as written, ending in E for east

explanation.surface: Spinning propellers are switching the course of a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: The E (east) at the end of ARE is changed to S (south).
explanation.definitionFit: Oars are the poles with blades that propel a rowing boat through the water.

clue.text: Frailty of the cat running out of its quota of lives

indicators.note: running outside something means going around it, enclosing it

blocks.note: puss is a name for a cat
a cat is said to have nine lives

explanation.surface: An old cat grows weak as it uses up its allotted lives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Running out of' seems to mean exhausting; it means the cat runs round the outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Puniness is smallness and weakness, the condition of being feeble or slight.

clue.text: A run can make the trainee totter

blocks.note: L is the learner, a trainee, from the L-plate
one who tots up figures adds them

explanation.surface: A sprint might leave the new recruit unsteady on their feet.
explanation.walkthrough: Totter looks like the verb to wobble; it is one who tots up. A run here is a ladder in tights or stockings.
explanation.definitionFit: A run in stockings is a vertical line of unravelled stitches, the British name for which is the answer.

clue.text: Separate country and town

blocks.note: to sunder is to split apart
a land is a country

explanation.surface: A political call to split the countryside from the town.
explanation.walkthrough: SUNDERLAND is a port in north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: Sunderland is an industrial port on the River Wear in north-east England, a large town in 1984.
